findings.title: Tool `create_entities` has unclear description (score 2/5)
findings.description: The description 'Create multiple new entities in the knowledge graph' is minimal and ambiguous. It doesn't explain what a 'knowledge graph' is in this context, what entities are for, when to use this tool, what valid entityType values are, or what observations should contain. While the schema shows the structure, the field-level descriptions are tautological ('The name of the entity', 'The type of the entity') and provide no actionable guidance. An agent would have to guess at appropriate usage patterns.

specific_issues: No explanation of what 'knowledge graph' refers to or its purpose
No guidance on when to use this tool vs. alternatives
No examples of valid entityType values or naming conventions
Field descriptions are circular/tautological ('name of the entity', 'type of the entity')
No description of what 'observations' represent or how they should be formatted
No mention of constraints (e.g., uniqueness of names, duplicate handling, max entities per call)
No indication of side effects or persistence behavior

findings.remediation: Rewrite description to clearly explain what the tool does, when to use it, and key constraints.

findings.title: Tool `read_graph` has unclear description (score 2/5)
findings.description: The description is extremely terse at just five words. While it conveys the basic action (reading the entire knowledge graph), it omits critical information: what 'knowledge graph' refers to in this context, what the returned structure looks like, when an agent should use this tool versus alternatives, performance considerations for large graphs, and what format the output takes. An agent would have to guess at usage patterns and could not anticipate the response shape.

specific_issues: No explanation of what the 'knowledge graph' contains or represents
No guidance on when to use this tool vs. a more targeted query
No description of the return value structure or format
No mention of performance/size considerations for reading the 'entire' graph
Empty input schema is fine, but no context on whether filters/pagination exist elsewhere

findings.remediation: Rewrite description to clearly explain what the tool does, when to use it, and key constraints.

findings.title: Tool `open_nodes` has unclear description (score 2/5)
findings.description: The description is minimal and ambiguous. It states what the tool does at a surface level ('open specific nodes in the knowledge graph by their names') but doesn't explain what 'opening' a node means (retrieve metadata? read contents? activate?), what a 'knowledge graph' refers to in this context, what data is returned, when to use this tool versus alternatives, or how node names are formatted/discovered. An agent would have to guess at usage.

specific_issues: 'Open' is undefined — unclear if it returns node data, contents, relationships, or all of the above
No context on what the 'knowledge graph' contains or where it comes from
No guidance on when to use this tool versus searching or listing nodes
No description of the return value/output shape
No information on how to discover valid node names (case sensitivity, format, namespace)
No mention of behavior when a name doesn't exist (error vs. silent skip)
Parameter description ('An array of entity names to retrieve') conflicts slightly with tool name ('nodes' vs 'entities')

findings.remediation: Rewrite description to clearly explain what the tool does, when to use it, and key constraints.
